models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Quiet night at Portorosa, light and benign through tomorrow; the weather arrives Sunday with WNW 4-5 ft seas in the islands.
briefing.synopsis: Light, rotating winds dominate the Tyrrhenian tonight - no organised gradient over the Aeolians. The consensus across available models has Portorosa at 3-5 kt, backing through S overnight and swinging WNW around midday Saturday, with waves holding 1.2-1.6 ft. From late Saturday night a WNW flow builds sharply: Portorosa goes to 11.9 kt WNW with gusts 28 kt and 4.2 ft seas by 06:00 Sunday (ECMWF IFS 0.25° / ECMWF WAM 0.25°, 09 Oct 12Z), and the outer islands fare worse - Filicudi 18.9 kt WNW and 4.9 ft at midnight Sunday, Salina and Lipari 5.2-5.3 ft at dawn. Models spread widely on the Sunday onset: Portorosa 06:00 ranges 5.6-16.8 kt between runs, so treat the timing as uncertain.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Portorosa Marina is the berth - enclosed, all-round shelter, scored sheltered on the 09 Oct 12Z data at 4.5 kt SE gusting 8.9 and 0.9 ft WNW swell. Overnight the breeze is light southerly, 3.8-4.7 kt at midnight and 06:00, with an interval-maximum gust of 23.7 kt in the 06:00 IFS field that is not supported by the mean - worth a glance at the lines but nothing more. Nothing in the payload would move the fleet off these berths tonight.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Saturday is benign at the berth: 4.2 kt SSW gusting 8.6 with 1.0 ft WNW swell, and the midday wind swinging WNW at around 4.7 kt - though the models disagree there, 2.5 to 8.6 kt. I have no leg scheduled or forecast for 10 October in this payload, so the plan reads as a second night at Portorosa Marina; if the fleet intends to move, any daylight window Saturday looks light-air motoring rather than sailing. If you are considering repositioning before Sunday, do it Saturday - the WNW build begins Saturday night and Sunday morning shows 4-5 ft seas across the island group.

passage_notes.note: Today's leg, verdict go, recommended 06:00 departure with deterioration after 11:00 (09 Oct 12Z data). The 12:00 window alone flagged caution on 24 kt gusts against an 11.3 kt mean; waves never above 1.0 ft. Logged here for the record - no further leg is forecast in this payload.

cautions: Sunday 11 Oct is the day to plan around: Portorosa 4.2 ft at 06:00, Filicudi 5.2 ft, Salina 5.2 ft, Lipari 5.3 ft, with gusts of 28-46 kt in the model fields. Onset timing is poorly agreed - Portorosa 06:00 Sunday spans 5.6-16.8 kt across models.

Several gust figures are interval maxima from a single model in near-calm air and should not be read as a forecast squall - Stromboli 65.1 kt against a 6.5 kt mean at 06:00 Saturday is the clearest example, with 42-47 kt similarly flagged at Salina and Filicudi.
Direction is unreliable in this light pattern - the stability record shows mean direction shifts of 55-62 degrees at 0-24 h lead. Do not plan a sail angle on tonight's wind direction.
briefing.confidence_note: Wind speed has been stable run to run (mean shift 1.8-2.0 kt out to 48 h across 23 snapshots) but direction swings by 46-62 degrees on average, and the models openly disagree on Saturday midday and the Sunday onset.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
